chapters.title: New kingdoms, Kakatiyas and the Delhi Sultanate (648–1325)
chapters.intro:
After Harsha many new dynasties rose (NCERT): Rashtrakutas, Palas and Pratiharas fought for Kanauj; the Cholas built an empire in the south; Mahmud of Ghazni raided the north; Prithviraj Chauhan fell to Muhammad Ghori; and the Delhi Sultanate began in 1206.

In Andhra the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi gave Telugu its first poet, Nannaya, and the Kakatiyas of Warangal — Ganapati Deva, Rudramadevi and Prataparudra — united the Telugu lands until 1323.

fragments.title: Kingdoms after Harsha
fragments.intro: The Arabs in Sind, the Palas, the Rashtrakutas and Ellora, the tripartite struggle for Kanauj, Shankaracharya and the rise of the Cholas.

fragments.title: Cholas, Ghaznavids and the rise of the Kakatiyas
fragments.intro: Tirumala, Mahmud of Ghazni, Rajendra Chola, Al-Biruni, Nannaya, Kulottunga I, Simhachalam, Basavanna, the Kakatiyas and Palnadu.

fragments.title: The Delhi Sultanate and the Kakatiya age
fragments.intro: Tarain, Aibak, Iltutmish, Raziyya, Balban, the Khaljis and Tughlaqs; Ganapati Deva, Rudramadevi, Marco Polo and the fall of Warangal.

takeaways: Rashtrakutas 753 (Dantidurga); Kailasa temple at Ellora (Krishna I); tripartite struggle for Kanauj (NCERT).
Rajaraja I (985) built Thanjavur's Brihadeshvara; Rajendra I took the Ganga and Srivijaya (NCERT).
Mahmud of Ghazni raided 17 times (1000–1025); Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind (NCERT).
Nannaya (Rajaraja Narendra) began Telugu literature; Kavitrayam: Nannaya, Tikkana, Errana.
Tarain 1191 and 1192 (NCERT); Delhi Sultanate from 1206 under Qutbuddin Aibak (NCERT).
chapters.source: NCERT Class 7 Our Pasts II; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 5 "Through the Eyes of Travellers"; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History II, Ch. 6 "Bhakti-Sufi Traditions"; Andhra Pradesh history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

pegs.hook: 712: the Arabs take Sind — the first Muslim rule in India.
985: Rajaraja I. Chola peak 985–1044 (Rajaraja and Rajendra).
1192: the second battle of Tarain; the Sultanate follows in 1206.
1206: the Delhi Sultanate begins; it lasts 320 years, to 1526.
1323: Warangal falls; Muhammad bin Tughlaq becomes Sultan two years later (1325).

chapters.title: Vijayanagara, the Mughals and the Qutb Shahis (1326–1755)
chapters.intro: After the Tughlaqs, power in the south passed to Vijayanagara (1336) and the Bahmanis (1347), and in Andhra to the Musunuri Nayakas, the Reddis and later the Qutb Shahis of Golconda (1518). In the north Babur founded the Mughal empire at Panipat (1526); Akbar built it; Aurangzeb stretched it to its limits and his death (1707) opened the age of new states — Hyderabad, Bengal, Awadh, the Marathas and the Sikhs (NCERT). Europeans arrived from 1498 and began to fight for the Carnatic.

fragments.title: Vijayanagara, Bahmanis and Reddis
fragments.intro: Ibn Battuta, the Musunuri Nayakas, Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis, Timur, Annamacharya and Potana, Guru Nanak, Vasco da Gama, Krishnadevaraya and the Qutb Shahis.

fragments.title: Babur to Akbar
fragments.intro: Panipat and Khanwa, Sher Shah, Panipat II, Talikota, the Ibadat Khana, Haldighati, Hyderabad and the East India Company.

fragments.title: Jahangir to Aurangzeb
fragments.intro: Masulipatnam, Thomas Roe, the Taj Mahal, Madras, Bernier, Shivaji and Purandar, the fall of Golconda, the Khalsa and Aurangzeb's death.

fragments.title: New states of the eighteenth century
fragments.intro: Banda Bahadur, the Peshwas, Bengal and Awadh, the Nizams of Hyderabad, Nadir Shah, Abdali and the Carnatic Wars.

takeaways: Ibn Battuta reached Sind in 1333 (NCERT); Vijayanagara 1336 (Harihara and Bukka); Bahmani 1347 (NCERT).
Qutb Shahis 1518; Hyderabad and Charminar 1591; Golconda fell 1687.
Shivaji crowned 1674; Khalsa 1699; Aurangzeb died 1707; Nadir Shah 1739; Asaf Jah 1724 (NCERT).

pegs.hook: 1526: Panipat-1 and the Mughals. Panipat years 1526, 1556, 1761.
1565: Talikota — Vijayanagara's capital falls after 229 years.
1707: Aurangzeb dies — the start of Mughal decline.
